record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: How should theoretical calculations and experimental analyses define and match centrality classes so that comparisons between heavy-ion data and models yield meaningful quantitative statements about quark-gluon-plasma transport coefficients, especially when impact parameter, initial gluon number, entropy production, and final particle yields must be related?

evidence.quote:
Some questions arose as to how a meaningful comparison to theory calculations can
and should be performed, which is crucial for any quantitative statements about the
transport coefficients of the quark gluon plasma.

This mapping procedure needs to be carefully cross-checked, especially when
the evolution is dissipative and the entropy increases. Differing centrality selection
criteria can significantly influence the results, and any assumptions relating the impact
parameter to the number of gluons and the final particle yields needs to be verified.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of consistently defining and matching centrality between heavy-ion experiments and hydrodynamic/transport models remains an active methodological issue in the field. Recent Bayesian analyses (e.g., JETSCAPE, Trajectum) explicitly treat centrality matching and its systematic uncertainty as part of the calibration, but no universally accepted, dissipation-aware prescription has been established; different initial-condition models still yield centrality-dependent biases in extracted η/s and ζ/s.

status_evidence.title: Bayesian calibration of QGP transport properties (JETSCAPE)
status_evidence.snippet: Centrality classes are defined by matching the simulated charged-particle multiplicity distribution to experimental data; residual systematic uncertainties from centrality definition are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Centrality matching is handled empirically and remains a source of systematic uncertainty in transport-coefficient extraction.

status_evidence.title: Trajectum: Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: The mapping between impact parameter, initial entropy, and final multiplicity is model-dependent and contributes to uncertainties in η/s and ζ/s.
status_evidence.claim: No universally agreed prescription; matching is performed model-by-model.
